page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8ae.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on a KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T34 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, configured with 1 physical core presenting 2 dedicated vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The CPU exposes instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI for accelerated cryptographic and vector tasks.

Hardware allocation pairs the 2 vCPUs with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes without bundled local storage (local storage size is listed as None) and does not feature hardware GPU acceleration. Networking is configured with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reflect the single-socket architectural density. Single-threaded performance demonstrates high capability, registering strong top-25% marks in stress-ng single-core (3111.99) and Geekbench single-core (1962.0). Conversely, aggregate parallel throughput falls into the bottom 25% bracket across Geekbench multi-core (2448.0) and PassMark CPU (3862.41), bounded directly by the 2-vCPU envelope. Memory bandwidth yields average mid-range throughput on larger uncached blocks (45.05 GB/sec read, 26.33 GB/sec write).

Given its high memory-per-core ratio and capable single-core instruction processing, ecs.r8ae.large delivers cost-efficient resource provisioning for small memory-intensive operations without requiring payment for excess vCPUs. Tradeoffs involve low overall multithreaded capacity and the requirement for external network-attached storage. Best-fit deployments include moderately sized in-memory caches, small databases, background queue workers, and lightweight memory-bound microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8ae.large is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at 3.4 GHz on the KVM hypervisor. Configured with 1 physical core and 2 dedicated vCPUs, it pairs 16.0 GB of RAM with a 3 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no bundled local storage and no GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight strong single-core compute performance, reaching top-tier results in single-threaded stress-ng and Geekbench tests, though total throughput is bounded by its 2-vCPU capacity, placing multi-threaded and database metrics in lower benchmark tiers. With 8.0 GB of memory per core, this instance offers an efficient resource balance for memory-sensitive tasks that do not need heavy multi-core concurrency, such as lightweight in-memory caching, microservices, and small database workloads.
